title: Stripe API pricing: plans, free tier and what to watch for
snippet:
Stripe is billed per transaction (2.9% + $0.30). It has a free tier: Unlimited test-mode sandbox (no CC); pay-per-transaction live. The paid plans we list start at 2.9% + 30¢ (Standard (pay-as-you-go, US online)).
## Plans and prices
| Plan | Price | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Standard (pay-as-you-go, US online) | 2.9% + 30¢ | Per successful online card charge; no setup or monthly fees. |
| In-person (Terminal, US) | 2.7% + 5¢ | Per successful in-person card payment. |
| Manually-keyed cards (US) | 3.4% + 30¢ | Per successful keyed-in card transaction. |
| ACH direct debit (US) | 0.8% (capped at $5) | Per ACH payment; disputes billed at $15 each. |
| Billing (subscriptions) | 0.7% of billing volume | Pay-as-you-go add-on; Tax add-on is 0.5% per transaction. |
| Custom / Enterprise | Contact sales | Interchange-plus (IC+) pricing, volume discounts, and multi-product discounts for large businesses. |
## How Stripe bills you
The pricing model is **per transaction (2.9% + $0.30)**. The reference-standard payments API: best-in-class docs, SDKs in every major language, official MCP server, and instant self-serve sandbox. Best suited to: developer-first payments platform.

title: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
snippet: The Queries API is free for all Stripe users through January 31, 2027. After that, you’ll pay per credit of API usage, with no monthly subscription required. The Reports API will remain free.

title: Hit with €15,000 Stripe API usage fees in 2 weeks; looking for tips & experiences
snippet:
Never heard of that before. The Stripe API should be free. The whole purpose of them giving us the API is so we can implement their system into ours and start processing payments to make Stripe money. That's entirely why Stripe charges the 3% transaction fee to cover any expenses that their system has such as running an API.
Totally agree on core payments: free to call, you pay per transaction. Our bill came from **Stripe Tax (Calculations API)** which **is metered**. The **API ref page doesn’t show prices**, so our devs (who live in refs) assumed “free like the rest.” Pricing sits on the Tax pricing page.

From all I know about Stripe API is that it’s FREE.
What you might have enabled is stripe Radar which is initially free for 30 days but then it’s per screen transaction.
If your devs have been hammering it, they need to be aware. It maybe just a hard leaning curve but if it’s from testing, that’s a lot of inefficient and wasted usage. Restrictions should be made to stop test/dev calls to it unless under stricter conditions.
